note: Recast from the description of the new species in Scheffrahn, Roisin, Wang, Bourguignon & Hellemans (2025), original in English; measurements follow the mean/max/min of Table 1 (n=5, two colonies), in mm; the alate is given in the original as Unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier monomorphic and small, the only species of the genus with a monomorphic soldier. It differs from the major soldiers of O. panamae and O. formosulus in having 6 long setae on the vertex, whereas those two species have numerous long and short setae scattered over the vertex; the head capsule in dorsal view is more pyriform than in the other two species. From the other monomorphic small nasute termites of Panama it differs in the reddish brown rather than yellow head capsule, antennal segments and maxillary palps; the nasus is broader and conical, with Coatitermes clevelandi the only exception. Within this group only this genus and Atlantitermes kirbyi have just 6 long setae on the head capsule, while the remaining taxa have dozens.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic and small. Head capsule reddish brown, nasus darker; antennal segments and maxillary palps reddish brown. Head capsule pyriform in dorsal view, constricted in the anterior third; in lateral view the head capsule is raised behind the antennal socket; 2 long setae at the apex of the vertex swelling and 4 long setae on the posterior half of the vertex. Nasus broadly conical, upturned about 10°. Antenna 11 segments, segment formula 2<3>4≤5. Mandibles with a small point. Measurements (n=5, mean/max/min): head length 1.25/1.30/1.20; head length to the base of the nasus 0.81/0.85/0.78; nasus length 0.43/0.45/0.40; maximum head width 0.72/0.78/0.68; head width at the posterior margin of the antennal socket 0.55/0.58/0.53; nasus width at midlength 0.10/0.10/0.10; maximum head height at the occipital margin 0.49/0.50/0.45; pronotum width 0.42/0.45/0.38; hind tibia length 0.87/0.90/0.83.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Holotype soldier in the University of Florida Termite Collection (UFTC) PN153; type locality El Cope National Park, Coclé province, Panama (8.6790, -80.5972), elevation 841 m, 2005-5-30, collected by J. Chase, numerous soldiers and workers taken beneath horse dung. Paratypes: Kuna Rd. Stop 4, Guna Yala (formerly San Blas), Panama (9.3261, 78.9992), elevation 360 m, 2010-6-5, collected by R. Scheffrahn, taken beneath a rotting branch. The specific name refers to the monomorphic soldier caste unique to this genus. Alate unknown.
